blocks.text: You can discover credentials from external identity sources (e.g., Active Directory (AD) or Entra ID). These discovered credentials can then be reviewed and moved depending on use cases.
Discovered credentials provide the following benefits and enable you to:

blocks.item: Reduce security risk by eliminating exposure of shared and long-lived privileged credentials, enforcing automated rotation.
Configure identity-centric access controls, such as Just-in-Time privileged access aligned with Zero Trust principles.

blocks.text: To learn more about Privileged Remote Access (PRA), see Understanding Privileged Remote Access. To set up PRA, see Step-by-Step Configuration Guide for Privileged Remote Access.
On the Discovered page (Zero Trust Browser > Credentials Management > Privileged Credentials > Discovered), you can do the following:

blocks.item: Add a new privileged credential.
Discover credentials from the AD.
Click the Filters icon to display or hide the filters.
Click the Search icon to locate specific information in the table.
Refresh the Discovered page to reflect the most current information.
Filter the information that appears in the table. By default, no filters are applied. To learn more, see Using Tables.

If you are using a Microtenant, then the Microtenant Ownership Type filter is available. By default, the Configured within Microtenant filter option is applied to show the privileged credentials configured within that specific Microtenant. The options for the filter are based on access type (Global and Configured within Microtenant). The Global option filters the information in the table that is configured within the Default Microtenant. The only available operator for this filter type is Equals.
View a list of all discovered credentials. For each discovered credential, you can see:

Name: The name of the discovered credential. Select the checkbox next to Name to select all credentials, or select the checkboxes of specific credentials to import or ignore them. You can also import and ignore individual credentials from the Actions column.
Credential Provider: The credential provider for the discovered credential (e.g., Active Directory, Entra ID, etc.).
Discovery Filter: The filters used to discover the credential.
Discovered: The date, time, and time zone when the credential was discovered.
Click the Import icon to import a discovered credential.
See instructions.
Select the following options in the Import Privileged Credentials window that appears:
Credential Class: Select a credential class from the drop-down menu.
Credential Pools: Select a credential pool from the drop-down menu.
Click Import.
Click the Delete icon to move the credential to the Ignored page. This action does not delete the credential from the external identity sources.
Modify the columns displayed in the table.
Display more rows or a different page of the table.
Go to the Managed page to manage privileged credentials.
Go to the Ignored page to manage discovered credentials that have been designated as ignored.
